requirements.title: Build a back-matter hash value
Build a back-matter rlink value
Build a back-matter resource value
Validate a standalone element against a named type
Element-type names are kebab-case and derived from the type names
An unknown element type is reported, not silently accepted
Error situations map to a fixed taxonomy
A non-raising validity check is available
Parse errors expose structured validation detail
A uniform facade wraps any document type
The facade reads common fields without type branching
The facade can be built from text, bytes, or a file
The assessment-period accessor is restricted to Assessment Plan and Assessment Results
Canonical type names derive from OSCAL name scopes, not from generator ordinals
Document wrapper names derive from each wrapper's single body field
Scalar root wrappers collapse to plain aliased types
Definitions that share a local name across modules get module-prefixed names
Union branches are named from the union and the property that only the branch has
Derivation guards abort on ambiguity, count mismatch, or uncovered collision
Models reject unknown fields (strict coverage)
The naming manifest is the shared source of truth across languages
Inline types are named from the canonical name of their parent and their own local name
Each enum site is a named type, marked open or closed
A property that holds one item or a list of items is a single-or-many type
Types deduplicate only for union-branch copies and explicit merges
A type is identified by JSON pointers into the complete schema
The manifest records each canonical type with its name, kind, and kind data
Canonical names are unique PascalCase identifiers
The store publishes a JSON Schema for each manifest file
The override data is the only hand-edited naming input
The manifest is generated from fixed inputs and is reproducible
Published names stay the same in later releases
A changed released name needs a breaking version increment
Parse an OSCAL document from text or bytes
Parse an OSCAL document from a file path
Typed parsers return the matching document type or report a type mismatch
Unknown fields are rejected during parsing
Input uses OSCAL property keys, not internal field names
Schema validation failures carry structured error detail
Regex patterns follow a defined portability rule
Timezone-aware datetimes are enforced where OSCAL requires them
Enum values are checked by the kind of the enum
Serialization emits OSCAL property keys
Serialization never emits null
Pretty output by default, compact output on request
Round-trip equivalence uses the shared canonical form
A datetime keeps its instant and offset
Bindings are namespaced by OSCAL major version
A binding is generated from exactly one active OSCAL release
The shared spec artifact uses Semantic Versioning for its own compatibility
The OSCAL release is recorded as Semantic Versioning build metadata
Spec artifacts are distributed pinned and hash-verified
